chunks.heading: This Website
chunks.text: Static site served entirely from AWS — the site is its own case study. Registered domain transferred from GoDaddy to Route 53 (including tearing down a stale DNSSEC chain — DS records deleted at the .dev registry before the nameserver cutover, so resolution never broke). Hosted from S3, fronted by CloudFront with a free ACM certificate. The .dev TLD is HSTS-preloaded, so every connection is HTTPS by force. Keyless CI/CD — OIDC-federated deploys, no stored credentials; every deploy verified byte-for-byte against the commit, behind three drift guards that run before any credential is assumed Security headers at the edge — a path-branched CSP: script-src 'none' on this page, which carries no JavaScript at all, and a separate narrow policy for the chatbot route Self-testing monitoring — alarm → SNS → Lambda → SES, with a monthly heartbeat that shares no failure modes with the path it tests Full write-ups and infrastructure code on GitHub → S3 CloudFront Route 53 ACM DNSSEC GitHub OIDC CloudFront Functions Lambda SES EventBridge Shipped

chunks.heading: Cloud Watchtower — macOS Menu-Bar Monitor
chunks.text: Source on GitHub → A native menu-bar app that answers two questions at a glance: is the site healthy, and what is it costing? CloudFront traffic and error rates, CloudWatch alarm state, and month-to-date spend against the budget. The menu-bar glyph encodes health, so the panel only needs opening when something is actually wrong. No dependencies at all — the AWS SDK for Swift is a 2.3 GB repository, so request signing is written directly instead: AWS SigV4 in about a hundred lines of CryptoKit, covering both the Query/XML and JSON wire protocols Cost is a design constraint — Cost Explorer bills per request, so it never runs on a timer and sits behind a button labelled with its own price; batching every metric into a single call brings the monitor to ~$0.12/month against roughly $8.50 for a poll-everything build — over 60× cheaper Least privilege — it assumes a scoped read-only role on one-hour STS credentials rather than holding the deploy key, and proves which identity it resolved instead of trusting the config Degrades honestly — a failed refresh keeps the last good value with the failure named and its age stated, and the glyph has a third state, because “cannot reach AWS” is not

chunks.heading: Retrieval-Augmented Chatbot on Amazon Bedrock
chunks.text: Ask the assistant a question → A RAG chatbot grounded in a corpus built from this site and the CV, so it answers from source text instead of hallucinating from general knowledge. Built alongside the AWS AI Practitioner track to understand the retrieval pipeline from the inside — chunking, embedding, and grounding — rather than treating the model as a black box. No vector database — the corpus is embedded with Titan v2 and cosine similarity runs inside the Lambda; a managed vector store at this scale is cost without benefit Answers cite their sources — the model sees only the retrieved chunks and is told to say it doesn't know rather than fill the gap Bounded by design — a public LLM endpoint is an unbounded bill, so per-IP and global caps in DynamoDB fail closed, and the visitor's question is passed to the model as data, never as instructions Amazon Bedrock Nova Lite Titan Embeddings RAG Lambda API Gateway DynamoDB Python Shipped

chunks.heading: Gmail & Drive Automation Suite
chunks.text: github.com/ryan-grey/gmail-drive-automation Google Apps Script suite that classifies, labels, and archives a 15+-year mailbox by year, plus rule-based cloud file organization. Engineered around Apps Script execution-time limits and the long tail of edge-case messages that break naive classifiers. Chunked, resumable runs bring the backlog under the six-minute execution ceiling that defeated the first version; permanent filters then classify new mail on arrival, so the structure holds without further passes. Google Apps Script Gmail API Drive API JavaScript In production

chunks.heading: AI-Assisted Commerce Operations
chunks.text: A working pipeline that runs a real multi-marketplace resale operation. End-to-end workflow automation for online resale: an image-processing pipeline (including a custom HEIC decoder built from format parsing + ffmpeg when standard libraries failed), automated market-comp research, listing copy generation, photo collage tooling for platform limits, and engagement-driven repricing across 40+ concurrent listings. Listing creation went from ~30 minutes of manual work to minutes; repricing decisions are driven by per-listing engagement data instead of guesswork. LLM agents Python Image processing Browser automation Pricing analytics
